name: Space Planner
tagline: Browser based space planning: draw rooms to scale, drop in furniture and desks, and share the layout.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified.

verdictSummary: The geometry here is not hard: a scaled 2D canvas, snapping, rectangles with real world dimensions, and a JSON save file cover most of what a person actually does with a space planner. An agent will get you a working single room layout tool in one sitting and a decent multi room one over a weekend. What it will not get you is the boring 80 percent that makes these products pleasant: a furniture catalog with correct dimensions, clean wall joins and door swings, printable scaled output, and a 3D view people can actually read. If you are laying out one office or one apartment once, build it. If you do this weekly for clients and hand deliverables to other humans, the polish is the product.
coreLoopDIY: A local web app where you draw walls to scale on a snapping grid, drop in dimensioned furniture and desk blocks, label and measure them, and export the plan as PNG, SVG, or JSON.
requirements: A list of your own item dimensions, since you will not have a furniture catalog
Optional: a printer or PDF export target if you want scaled paper plans
whatYouLose: A curated furniture and fixture library with real manufacturer dimensions
3D or isometric views that non technical people can actually interpret
Clean architectural drawing conventions: wall thickness, door swings, window symbols, dimension lines
Shared links, comments, and version history for the people you are planning the space with
Mobile and tablet editing, which is where measuring actually happens
moatNotes: The asset catalog is the quiet moat. Correct dimensions for thousands of real objects is data entry nobody wants to redo, and some of it is licensed from manufacturers.
whyPeopleStillPay: Because a plan is a deliverable. People pay so the output looks credible to a landlord, a contractor, a facilities team, or a client, and so they can send a link instead of a screenshot of their side project. The drawing engine is commodity; the catalog, the scaled print output, and the fact that it renders the same in someone else's browser are what is being bought.
notes: Great one-shot if you are the only person who ever has to read the plan.
prompt:
Build a local-first 2D space planner as a single page web app. No accounts, no backend, no telemetry.

Stack, non negotiable:
- Vite + React + TypeScript
- Plain SVG for the canvas, no canvas2d, no three.js, no paid libraries
- Zustand for state, Tailwind for styling
- Everything persists to localStorage, plus explicit JSON import/export

Core features:
1. A scaled worksheet: user sets units (feet+inches or meters) and a scale, with a snapping grid at a configurable increment.
2. Wall drawing: click to place wall segments, snap to grid and to existing endpoints, configurable wall thickness, closed loops render as rooms with a computed floor area.
3. Items: rectangular objects with a name, width, depth, rotation, and color. Drag, rotate in 15 degree steps, nudge with arrow keys, snap edges to walls and to other items.
4. A small built-in item palette I define in a local TypeScript file: desk, chair, table, sofa, bed, bookshelf, door, window. Each has default dimensions I can override per instance. Make this file trivially extendable.
5. Dimension labels: toggle to show width x depth on every item, and running dimensions along walls.
6. Layers: walls, furniture, annotations. Toggle visibility and lock per layer.
7. Text annotations placed anywhere on the plan.
8. Multiple plans stored locally in a sidebar list, each renameable and duplicable.
9. Export: PNG at 2x, SVG, and JSON. Import the JSON back.
10. Print stylesheet that outputs the plan at true scale on Letter and A4 with a scale bar.

Explicitly out of scope: 3D rendering, real furniture catalogs, collaboration, sharing links, cloud sync, auth, mobile editing (make it usable read-only on small screens and leave it there).

Quality bar: undo/redo with at least 50 steps, keyboard shortcuts (v select, w wall, t text, delete, cmd+z, cmd+shift+z), no dropped drags, and no layout shift when the sidebar opens. Ship a README with run instructions and a seeded example plan of a 12ft by 14ft home office so the app is not empty on first load.
